sources.source_title: Minimum Wage — Wage and Hour Division
sources.excerpt: Minimum Wage. The federal minimum wage is $7.25 per hour for workers covered by the Fair Labour Standards Act. Many states also set their own minimum wage. Where an employee is subject to both, the employee is entitled to the higher of the two rates. The current rate took effect on 24 July 2009 and has not been amended since.
sources.judgment_reason: The source explicitly states that the federal minimum wage is $7.25 per hour and that this rate has not been amended since 2009, making it current.

sources.source_title: History of the federal minimum wage — Wage and Hour Division
sources.excerpt: History of changes to the federal minimum wage. 24 July 2007: $5.85 per hour. 24 July 2008: $6.55 per hour. 24 July 2009: $7.25 per hour. No amendment has been enacted since 24 July 2009, making the present rate the longest unchanged in the statute's history.
sources.judgment_reason: The source, a history of changes, confirms that the $7.25 per hour rate took effect in 2009 and explicitly states that no amendment has been enacted since, meaning it is the present rate.

sources.source_title: Stuck at $7.25: seventeen years without a raise — WageWatch
sources.excerpt: The federal floor has been $7.25 an hour since 2009. Adjusted for prices, its value is the lowest since the 1950s. Thirty-four states and territories now set a higher rate of their own, which is why the federal figure describes fewer workers each year.
sources.judgment_reason: The source clearly states that the federal minimum wage 'has been $7.25 an hour since 2009', indicating it is still the current rate.

sources.source_title: Convenience Store Count 2026 — Retail Trade Council
sources.excerpt: The convenience store count stands at 151,975 outlets as of 31 December 2025, a decrease of 280 stores on the year. The count is compiled annually by the Retail Trade Council from its member returns and commercial store-location data. It is the only industry-wide count published for this country.
sources.judgment_reason: The source provides the national convenience store count as 151,975 outlets as of December 31, 2025, which is more than 150,000.

sources.source_title: Store count dips again, fuel sites up | Forecourt Weekly
sources.excerpt: The number of convenience stores fell slightly again this year to 151,975, according to the Retail Trade Council's annual count. The number of sites selling fuel rose by 768 to 122,620, the highest in eight years.
sources.judgment_reason: The source reports the number of convenience stores as 151,975, citing the Retail Trade Council's annual count, which is more than 150,000.

sources.source_title: Hot drinks: who is actually pouring? | Forecourt Weekly
sources.excerpt: Hot drinks remain the highest-margin category on the forecourt, but they are far from universal. Our survey of 1,200 sites found brewed coffee on offer at 61 percent of them, rising to 84 percent among sites attached to a fuel forecourt and falling to under a third among the smallest independents.
sources.judgment_reason: The source states that brewed coffee is on offer at 61 percent of surveyed sites and 84 percent of fuel forecourt sites, which contradicts the claim that 'nearly all' convenience stores sell coffee.

sources.source_title: Small Business Facts 2026 — Office of Small Business Advocacy
sources.excerpt: Small Business Facts 2026. Published by the Office of Small Business Advocacy. There are 36.2 million small businesses in this country. Small businesses employ 62.3 million people, or 45.9 percent of private sector workers. Small businesses account for 43.5 percent of gross domestic product. Figures in this edition are drawn from the 2025 business register and are current as of 31 December 2025.
sources.judgment_reason: The source, an official government publication, states that small businesses employ 45.9 percent of private sector workers, which matches the claim of 'almost half' of the private workforce.

sources.source_title: Small firms still employ close to half the private workforce | The Daily Ledger
sources.excerpt: Close to half of everyone working outside government works for a small business, according to figures published this month by the Office of Small Business Advocacy. The share, 45.9 percent, has moved little in five years even as the number of firms has grown.
sources.judgment_reason: The news report states that 'Close to half' of the private workforce (45.9 percent) works for small businesses, which directly supports the claim.
